name: Large-scale Attribute Dataset for Zero-shot Learning
description: Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) has attracted huge research attention over the past few years; it aims to learn the new concepts that have never been seen before. In classical ZSL algorithms, attributes are introduced as the intermediate semantic representation to realize the knowledge transfer from seen classes to unseen classes. Previous ZSL algorithms are tested on several benchmark datasets annotated with attributes. However, these datasets are defective in terms of the image distribution and attribute diversity. In addition, we argue that the "co-occurrence bias problem" of existing datasets, which is caused by the biased co-occurrence of objects, significantly hinders models from correctly learning the concept. To overcome these problems, we propose a Large-scale Attribute Dataset (LAD). Our dataset has 78,017 images of 5 super-classes, 230 classes. reputation: A notable dataset in zero-shot learning research, especially for studying attribute-based transfer and reducing dataset bias.
notes: Non-LLM computer vision benchmark; results are sensitive to the chosen seen/unseen split and protocol, and the field has many competing ZSL datasets and evaluation settings.
